research_question: Does the hybrid electromechanical alignment (delta_sys + residual + lag-aware) close the MMECG continuous ECG gap while preserving Shape-200 morphology?
hypothesis: On MMECG fold_01, adding delta_sys (B1), then residual (B3), then lag-aware (B4) progressively increases full-window PCC and improves RR/R-F1 while Shape-200 PCC stays roughly flat, versus the WSST-TCN floor (B0).
protocol: Fold-01 strict LOSO minimal-loop ablation, WSST input, 50 epochs, no target-subject calibration.
baseline: B0 = WSST-TCN floor (model_arch=wsst_tcn, same training settings).
changed_variable: Alignment components toggled on one backbone: B1 +delta_sys; B3 +delta_sys+residual; B4 +delta_sys+residual+lag-aware. All other settings fixed.
controlled_variables: MMECG processed/loso fold_01 strict LOSO split
lag (B4 only): lag_max_ms=40, lambda_lag_pcc=0.05, lambda_lag_l1=0.01, lambda_zero_pcc=0.05, lambda_lag_penalty=0.02
success_criteria: All four arms complete on fold_01.
B4 full-window (rem_full_ola) PCC clearly improves over B0 and over the prior refine baseline 0.420.
Shape-200 PCC on B1/B3/B4 stays roughly flat (not dropping meaningfully below ~0.87).
RR / R-F1 improve from B0 -> B4.
go_no_go: If B4 continuous does not clearly improve on fold_01, stop-loss or adjust the alignment design before scaling. If it clearly improves, extend to 11-fold LOSO + CR_RVS.
checkpoint_selection: Validation-best checkpoint only; no test-set selection.
estimated_compute: Four fold-01 runs, 50 epochs each, one GPU.
failure_interpretation: If delta_sys/residual/lag do not separably help continuous metrics, dense-decoder alignment is insufficient; pivot to explicit cycle assembly from the Shape-200 head.
